speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help narrow down the cause, are you experiencing any neck pain, numbness in your hand, or any recent trauma to the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (with significant confounding factors including diabetes and anabolic steroid use).

Given the history of dropping objects, weight loss, and steroid use, I am highly suspicious of a more systemic or compressive etiology such as a paraspinal mass or severe diabetic neuropathy mimicking focal weakness. REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical_Spine. REQUEST IMAGES.
